To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gel rheology in a viscometers is consistent with gel rheology during gel extrusion in fractures.

gel extrusion through a fracture can be described using the Darcy equation, that the resistance factor (RF) for a given gel depends on the injection velocity, that the pressure gradient to inject a gel through a 0.1 cm diameter fracture is ~10-15 psi, and that the gel's rheological behavior is consistent with that of a gel-like material.
gel rheology is important to understanding gel extrusion in fractures, and that gel rheology measurements can be used to predict gel extrusion through a fracture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a conformance control technology that can be used to reduce fluid production in fractured reservoirs.
the development of a new technique for conformance control.
developing and evaluating new gels for conformance control in fractures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the gel is elastic, the elastic component dominates over the viscous component, the elastic modulus increases with increasing polymer concentration, the elastic modulus is insensitive to injection velocity, the gel is shear thinning, and the gel is temperature dependent.
the rheological properties of the gels are such that they are easily extruded through the fractures.
the rheology of gels used for conformance control in fractures is consistent with the behavior of a viscoelastic gel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gel extrusion through a fracture is a viscoelastic process.
gels used for conformance control in fractures are elastic, with a shear-thinning behavior.
the rheological behavior of gels is consistent with the observations made during gel extrusion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gel rheology in the fracture is dominated by the elastic component of the gel.
gels used for conformance control are highly elastic.
the elastic nature of the gel is the main reason why the gels can be extruded through fractures.
